figures.caption: Fig. 1 | Monumental developments of HSEs over the years. These summaries correspond to the important reports on the developmental history of halogen-containing solid electrolytes (HSEs) from 1923 when LiAlCl4 as HSE was reported. Specifically shown in the figure are the crystal structures of the beginnings of each new HSE and its typical compounds. ASSB, all-solid-state battery; RT, room temperature; SEs, solid electrolytes.

figures.caption: Fig. 3 | Liquid-phase preparation procedures, typical structures and ion transport mechanisms in the Li-M-X system. a, Typical water-mediated synthesis for Li3InCl6 SEs and ammonium-assisted synthesis for Li3MCl6 (M = Y, Sc, Er) SE. b, The formation of Li3MX6 SE and its hopping mechanism. c,d,e, Crystal structures of monoclinic LiAlCl4 (c); inverse spinel Li2MCl4 (d); deficient inverse-spinel Li2Sc2/3Cl4 (e). f, ccp anion framework Li3MCl6 (M = Sc, In) and Li3M(Br,I)6 with migration pathways. g, hcp anion framework Li3MCl6 (M = Er, Y, Ho, Yb).

figures.caption: Fig. 4 | Main preparation procedures, crystallography and ion transport pathways of LPSX-type HSEs (Li2S-P2S5-LiX system). a, Typical solid-phase sintering and liquid-phase method. b, The formation and crystal structure of Li6PS5X and a face-sharing S3X2 double tetrahedron containing Li1 and Li2. c, The local pathway cages in Li6PS5Cl and Li6PS5I. d, Three possible jump processes (dark-blue arrows) for lithium ions (Wyckoff positions 24g and 48h). e, Crystal structure of delta-Li3PS4. f, Crystal structure of Li4PS4I.

figures.caption: Fig. 6 | Performance analysis of experimentally assembled cells based on halogen-containing solid electrolytes. Comparison of the specific capacity test data of all-solid-state batteries assembled with various electrolytes at different current densities. SEs, solid electrolytes.

Fig. 7 | Interfacial composition and chemical stability of HSEs. a,b, Chemical stability of SE-coated cathode materials (a) and composite cathode materials (b). c,d, Interfacial stability of Li3MX6-type SEs (c) and Li6PS5X-type SEs (d) towards lithium metal anode (LMA). e, Li-M-X SE with the LPSX-type SE as a thin buffer layer towards the LMA. f, Void formation and lithium dendrite growth from poor interfacial contact between Li6PS5Cl SE and LMA, and interfacial modifications.
